subject: VM evidence: scan cadence, SLA attestations, and exception request
messages:
From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@fintegrate.com>
To: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vulnerability evidence request for SOC 2 audit - quick turnaround requested

Hi Priyom,

We are coming up on the SOC 2 fieldwork window and need to collect up-to-date vulnerability management evidence from vendors. Specifically, can you provide: 

- Your current authenticated scan cadence and proof-of-execution for the last 30 days (internal and external scans).
- SLA commitments for CVE remediation (critical/important/medium thresholds and corresponding time-to-remediate).
- Evidence for ownership/mitigation for a specific issue we found: CVE-2027-10234 (third-party library in your nimbus worker image).

Requested delivery: signed attestation and scan artifacts by 2027-04-21 EOD. If you need an exception, please provide a compensating-control plan and remediation timeline.

Can you route this to the person who owns VM evidence? CCing our audit team is fine.

Thanks,
Morgan Lee
Security Assurance Manager
Fintegrate

(Prefers PDF or CSV attachments; if you use a secure Drive link, please ensure it has a time-limited token.)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@fintegrate.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Vulnerability evidence request for SOC 2 audit - quick turnaround requested

Hi Morgan — thanks for the heads up. Attaching a compact evidence packet and an attestation draft. Key points up front: 

- Scan cadence: authenticated weekly scans against internal fleet (agent-based), external attack-surface scans weekly (agentless), and a monthly full-surface scan (external+internal) with baseline CVE correlation.
- SLA: Critical (CVSS>=9.0) — initial remediation plan + rollback window within 72 hours; High (7.0-8.9) — 7 calendar days; Medium (4.0-6.9) — 30 calendar days. We log exceptions and close with compensating controls where appropriate.
- Evidence: attached vm-scan-index-20270418.csv (export of last 6 runs), scan-summary-20270418.pdf (scan highlights + remediation tickets), and a proposed mitigation plan for CVE-2027-10234 (cve-2027-10234-mitigation-plan.pdf).

We also propose to provide a time-limited scanner credential (read-only) so you can perform a one-time verification scan. If you prefer, we can export raw scan output and Nessus/Qualys/Trivy reports for the audit team.

If you accept the SLA language above we will sign the attestation and return it. If you need a formal exception for CVE-2027-10234 (it's a transitive dependency in an upstream open-source package), we have a short compensating-control proposal below: short-lived pinned patchbackport, network segregation for affected workers, and a temporary WAF rule. Proposed remediation ETA: 30 calendar days from today if you approve the exception.

Attachments: vm-scan-index-20270418.csv, scan-summary-20270418.pdf, cve-2027-10234-mitigation-plan.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through artifacts.

— Priyom
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
pri...@redwoodinference.com

Thanks, Priyom — got the packet and attachments. A few clarifying points and a request for an exception log:

On Mon, Apr 19, 2027 at 11:42 AM Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> - SLA: Critical (CVSS>=9.0) — initial remediation plan + rollback window within 72 hours; High (7.0-8.9) — 7 calendar days; Medium (4.0-6.9) — 30 calendar days.

We can accept those SLAs for vendor evidence, but we need explicit ownership for CVE-2027-10234. Our scans flagged it as present in your nimbus worker image via the open-source package chain. Can you confirm: 

1) Which team owns remediation (runtime infra / build pipeline / third-party dependency team)?
2) If you are requesting an exception, please provide a formal exception entry with compensating controls and a PR/issue link that tracks the backport work.

Also, for SOC 2 we prefer to see weekly authenticated scan outputs in CSV or JSON (not just summary PDFs). Can you include raw output for the last two authenticated runs?

If you can send the exception log + raw run exports by EOD 2027-04-21, we should be able to include this in our evidence pack.

Best,
Morgan
Security Assurance Manager, Fintegrate

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@fintegrate.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Vulnerability evidence request for SOC 2 audit - quick turnaround requested

Morgan — quick update and formal exception request below. Quoting the ownership ask: our Runtime/Infrastructure teams own the nimbus worker images (laura.bennett is the exec sponsor). We have created internal ticket RW-3542 to land a backport for the vulnerable library and a PR link is included in the attached mitigation plan.

Exception request (formal):
- CVE: CVE-2027-10234 
- Scope: Transitive dependency in nimbus-worker image versions 3.2.0 - 3.4.1 (non-production Canary nodes excluded).
- Compensating controls in place: network-segmentation (isolated worker VPC), temporary WAF rule to block exploitation vector, increased process-level auditing for the affected binary, and a rollout hold for non-critical clusters.
- Proposed remediation timeline: 30 calendar days from 2027-04-21 (complete by 2027-05-21).
- Verification: we will provide a follow-up authenticated scan and the PR that contains the backport/upgrade.

Raw exports: I have placed two recent authenticated-scan exports in the Drive link below and included a CSV index (attached). If you prefer we can attach raw JSON too; let me know.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-example-soc2-evidence (time-limited token)

If this satisfies your audit requirement we request the exception be accepted pending final remediation. Happy to hop on a short call to go over the PR and evidence.

— Priyom
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: vm-scan-index-20270418.csv (index to raw runs), cve-2027-10234-mitigation-plan.pdf
